name: Manual reverse-reverb swell: reverse, print 100%-wet reverb, re-reverse, trim and fade into the onset
goal: Make a reverse-reverb swell by hand (no dedicated plugin) that leads into a vocal, chord or hit with its own timbre: duplicate and reverse the source, print a large 100%-wet reverb of the reversed audio, keep only the part that leads into the first word/hit, reverse it back so it swells forward, normalize, align and fade it into the dry onset, and optionally give the swell its own late-automated reverb tail.

source.title: Reverse Reverb Technique, Tips and Tricks in Cubase Music Production Tutorial

prerequisites: DAW (or offline renderer) with audio reverse, bounce/export, normalize and clip fades

inputs.name: source_audio
inputs.description: Vocal phrase, chord, kick, crash, noise rise - the element the swell leads into

outputs.name: reverse_swell
outputs.description: Printed swell clip placed before the source onset

steps.action: Duplicate the source audio onto a second track.
Insert a large reverb (large live-stage/hall size) on that track with mix at 100% so you hear only the wet signal.
Bounce/export the soloed wet signal to a new audio file (mono in the source example).
Keep only the part that matters - the portion that leads into the first word/hit - and delete the rest and the temporary track.
Reverse the printed clip back so the reverb now swells forward into the onset, and normalize it.
steps.expect: Swell that rises toward the source

steps.action: Move it to just before the dry source and add short fade-in/fade-out at the clip edges to remove clicks.
steps.expect: Swell lands on the onset without clicks

steps.action: Optional: put another reverb (~50% mix) on the swell channel so it has a softer tail, and automate that reverb to come in only at the last split second so the whole tail does not wash out.
steps.expect: Swell blends into the source without smearing it

steps.action: Reuse on other sources: kick, cymbal crash into a breakdown, white-noise rise, pads/chords.

verification: Swell peak arrives at (not after) the source onset
No click at the swell clip start/end
Swell carries the timbre of the element it introduces
Optional tail reverb does not muddy the dry phrase
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Web Audio mapping: OfflineAudioContext render -> reverse the AudioBuffer -> ConvolverNode 100% wet render -> reverse again -> schedule so it ends at the source onset.
Distinct from reverb-pads-type-choice-and-send-setup and shimmer-reverb-pitchshift-plus12-feedback: this is the print-reverse-print swell technique.
